one_line: Poet-scholars of Sultanate Bengal whose vernacular epics helped make Bengali a major literary language.

appearance.age_look: Both look in their mid-40s; Krittibas is slightly lean and wiry, Maladhar broader-shouldered and sturdier.
appearance.face: Krittibas has an oval face, medium-brown complexion, sharp nose, high cheekbones, thin moustache and calm, introspective eyes with a thoughtful half-smile; Maladhar has a squarer jaw, slightly lighter brown complexion, fuller moustache, gentle smile and lively, confident eyes.
appearance.hair: Both wear their black hair oiled and neatly parted, tied back in a short low knot; Krittibas has a simple white cotton headcloth wrapped as a narrow turban band around the crown, while Maladhar has a slightly wider pale yellow cloth band with a subtle woven border.
appearance.costume: Krittibas wears a mid-15th-century Bengali scholar’s outfit: a knee-length white cotton jama (front-opening tunic with side ties) with simple narrow cuffs, over an ankle-length off-white dhoti tied in the Bengali style with pleats in front; a thin, unpatterned, soft white cotton uttariya (shawl) drapes from his left shoulder across his chest and around his forearm, and his feet are in plain dark brown leather mojari shoes, all fabrics looking slightly worn but clean; Maladhar wears a similar jama in warm light cream with a fine maroon woven edge at collar and cuffs, over a pale mustard-yellow dhoti with a narrow maroon border at the hem, and a richer deep red cotton uttariya with a subtle gold-toned woven stripe along its edges wrapped from right shoulder across his chest and around his waist, with slightly more polished dark brown mojari shoes hinting at elite patronage, both outfits in plain woven cotton typical of Sultanate Bengal with no modern prints.
appearance.signature: Krittibas carries a rolled palm-leaf manuscript tied with a thin red cord in his left hand, while Maladhar holds a slightly larger bound stack of palm leaves with wooden covers under his right arm, both inscribed with fine script but shown as abstract lines.

ref_desc: Two mid-40s Bengali poets stand together: Krittibas lean in white jama, off-white dhoti and white shawl with narrow white headband holding a rolled palm-leaf manuscript, Maladhar sturdier in cream jama, mustard dhoti, deep red shawl, pale yellow headband and stacked palm-leaf book, all in white, cream, deep red, mustard and dark brown tones.
sheet_prompt: Draw a full-body anime-style character pair from 15th-century Sultanate Bengal: Krittibas Ojha, lean and thoughtful, medium-brown oval face with thin moustache, oiled black hair tied in a short low knot under a narrow white cotton headband, wearing a knee-length white cotton jama over an ankle-length off-white Bengali dhoti, a simple white cotton uttariya draped from left shoulder across his chest and forearm, and plain dark brown mojari shoes, holding a rolled palm-leaf manuscript tied with a thin red cord; beside him Maladhar Basu, broader-shouldered with a slightly lighter brown complexion and fuller moustache, similarly tied-back black hair under a slightly wider pale yellow cloth headband with a subtle border, wearing a cream jama with fine maroon edging at collar and cuffs, a pale mustard-yellow dhoti with a narrow maroon hem, and a deep red cotton uttariya with a gold-toned woven stripe wrapped from right shoulder across his chest and around his waist, matching dark brown mojari shoes, and a stacked palm-leaf manuscript with wooden covers under his arm; show them standing side by side, clearly displaying faces, hair, headcloths, layered garments, footwear, and manuscripts, in a coherent palette of white, cream, deep red, mustard yellow, and dark brown with dignified scholarly, shonen-anime energy.
